lots.what_it_is: Unknown Warrior Centenary 1920 Heritage Gold Sovereign Set, set 31 of 49. It holds a 1920 George V gold sovereign (mint not confirmed, most likely Perth) and a coloured 2020 UK 5 pound cupro-nickel coin, in a case with certificate and booklet. This is a private marketing set, not a Royal Mint product.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: the certificate reads 'Limited to just 49 sets of which this is set number 31', signed Linda MacLennan, General Manager. Photo 4: date 1920 with B.P. initials to the right. The mint letter on a 1920 sovereign sits on the ground line. I enlarged that area and could not see an M, P or S, but the photo is only 450 x 600 px, so this settles nothing. London struck no sovereigns in 1920, so the coin must be from Melbourne, Perth or Sydney. Perth is by far the most common and a 1920 Sydney is a major rarity. Photo 5: George V obverse, crisp, light wear on the high points. Photos 6-7: 2020 5 pound, 'Lest We Forget', coloured poppies, in a capsule. The box, plaque and booklet are present.
lots.condition: The sovereign is lightly circulated, about EF, with no visible damage or mount marks. Box and papers look complete. Weight and mint letter are not confirmed.

lots.working: Keep: the lowest same-item SOLD is Lugosi at AUD 800 (Feb 2025). 800 / 1.198 = 667.8, rounded down to 665. Flip: likely resale from SOLD evidence AUD 800, less 12% selling fees (AUD 96) and AUD 15 tracked postage = 689. 689 / 2.396 = 287.6, rounded down to 285. Big caveat: the current Gowans bid is already AUD 1,000, above both figures. The rule-based numbers rest on a sale made when gold was far cheaper. The gold alone is worth about AUD 1,412 at today's spot, so a hammer of AUD 1,175 (AUD 1,408 all-in) is roughly break-even on melt. Going above 665 is a call on the gold price, not something the SOLD evidence supports.
lots.confidence_reason: The set and date are clearly read and two same or close SOLD results were opened. lots.working: I follow the precedent used for lot 66 (another Max Angus in this sale): close same-artist, same-medium Hobart SOLD results within 24 months stand in for 'same item', since a painting is unique. Keep: lowest close SOLD within 24 months = Colville AUD 600 (10 Mar 2026); 600 / 1.198 = 500.8, round down = $500 (all-in $599). The sheet looks clean, with a warm line at the window edge that is likely the mount bevel or mild mat burn. The mount looks slightly toned. The back is not shown.

Photo 1 enlarged: five graduated old-cut diamonds in a carved scroll half hoop, with the centre stone largest. All five stones appear present. The stones look small (my estimate about 0.25-0.4ct in all, which cannot be confirmed from the photos) and a bit dull. The carved gallery and claws look worn but intact. Only one angle is shown, from the side at low resolution, so chips, claw wear and the underside cannot be judged.
lots.condition: Worn antique, all stones apparently present. Claw security, chips to the diamonds and shank thickness cannot be judged from two photos.
